body.prompt: Night inside a Roman emperor's campaign tent in 175 AD. Close-up at table height: an older man's weathered right hand, wearing a plain gold signet ring, slowly lowering a rolled papyrus letter tied with a cord and closed with an UNBROKEN red wax seal into a small round bronze brazier on a tripod. Several other sealed, unopened letters already lie in the brazier, their edges curling and glowing orange, small calm flames and drifting sparks rising. Behind, out of focus: the dark canvas wall of the tent, a folded deep-red general's cloak and a bronze helmet on a wooden stool. The fire is the only light source, warm orange light on the hand and the seal. The man's face is NOT in the frame — only the hand, forearm sleeve of dark wool, the letters and the brazier. The seals must be intact: the letters were never opened. Historically accurate Roman objects: papyrus rolls, wax seals, bronze tripod brazier; no books, no paper envelopes, no candles in modern holders. Cinematic oil-painting look, like a dark Renaissance chiaroscuro painting brought to life, deep warm shadows, muted bronze, umber and deep navy palette, fine film grain, painterly texture, vertical 9:16 frame, main subject in the lower half, a calm dark empty area in the top third for text. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, nothing modern anywhere.

The hand releases the sealed letter into the brazier and slowly withdraws out of frame; the flames gently catch the papyrus edge, it curls and glows, sparks drift upward, the fire light flickers softly on the tent wall. The camera stays still with only a very slow push-in toward the brazier. Keep the painterly look and every detail identical to the first frame; the wax seals stay unbroken. No faces, no extra hands or fingers, no explosions or big flames, no text, no camera shake, no cuts.
